inventory.title: Toronto Centreline (TCL)
inventory.join_role: spine: one output row per road segment (50,027 of 64,392 features; trails, rivers, railways and walkways excluded)
inventory.notes: Carries the street name, road class, one-way flag and address ranges for both sides of every segment. It does not carry the street's parking itself: no lane counts, no parking side, no stall positions.

inventory.title: Traffic and Parking By-Law Schedules
inventory.geometry: None (text; 52.9% of kept rules carry one intersection anchor point)
inventory.join_role: rules layer: 27,768 current street parking rules flattened to CSV and counted per street name
inventory.notes: Chapter 950 schedules. One JSON resource of 806.5 MB holds all 77,940 regulation records, current and repealed. Locations are legal text (street, side, between). Times are text ('Anytime', '7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., Mon. to Fri.'). No segment geometry in any record.

inventory.title: Parking Tickets
inventory.join_role: observed enforcement: 6,454,695 tickets (2023-2025 reference slice) aggregated by street name and attached to every segment of the street
inventory.notes: The enforcement record is fully open. Tickets locate to a street address; the reference project geocoded 86.9% of the slice to address points.

inventory.title: On-Street Permit Parking Area Maps
inventory.join_role: permit layer: segment midpoint in polygon test against 97 permit-area polygons
inventory.notes: Permit areas are polygons with area codes (e.g. 12B). The file names the areas; permit rules (hours, prices) are not in it.

inventory.title: Bikeways
inventory.join_role: frozen duplicate of the cycling network: the record's refresh rate is 'Will not be Refreshed', and the file is not the same as Cycling Network (1,323 features vs 1,581, different segment IDs). The maintained Cycling Network file was joined instead
inventory.notes: Kept in the inventory because a search for the bike network returns both records and nothing states which is canonical.

inventory.title: Cycling Network
inventory.join_role: bike layer: on-road lines within 25 m of a segment with the same street name set the segment's bike_infra_type (923 on-road features of 1,581)
inventory.notes: The maintained cycling network record (semi-annual refresh, modified 2026-09-14). Off-road multi-use trails were excluded from the join because they do not occupy a parking lane.

inventory.title: Green P Parking
inventory.join_role: facility layer: 252 car parks with address, capacity and rate text; segment rows count car parks within 250 m and distance to the nearest
inventory.notes: CKAN refresh rate is 'Will not be Refreshed': the resource used is the 2019 snapshot. Rates are text strings (e.g. '$2.50 / Half Hour'), not numbers with units. Off-street only.

inventory.title: Parking Occupancy
inventory.join_role: use layer: joined to Green P car parks by car park number (CP52 style); latest quarter kept
inventory.notes: Average daily peak occupancy per TPA off-street facility by quarter. Off-street only: there is no equivalent for on-street spaces.

inventory.title: Bike Share Toronto
inventory.join_role: 1,070 stations from the GBFS station_information feed the dataset points to; segment rows count stations within 250 m
inventory.notes: The CKAN entry is a pointer to the live GBFS feed, not a file. Station capacity is in the feed.

inventory.title: CaféTO Locations
inventory.join_role: 287 of 1,636 locations are parking-lane cafés or parklets; segment rows count them within 250 m
inventory.notes: CaféTO locations record the season's licensed parking-lane and sidewalk cafés. CKAN excerpt calls them historical locations.

inventory.title: Off-Street Parking – Surface Lots – Accessible Stalls
inventory.join_role: 669 accessible stalls at TPA surface lots; segment rows count them within 250 m
inventory.notes: Stall-level coordinates exist here, but only for accessible stalls in off-street surface lots. Source note says positions come from 2024 aerial photography.

inventory.title: Taxicab Stand Locations
inventory.join_role: February 2014 snapshot, no coordinates: street, side and a text location per stand. The current stands are in the by-law schedules (Schedule 05, 159 current rules), which were joined instead
inventory.notes: 112 stands listed. The dataset is 12 years stale relative to the by-law file.

inventory.title: The City Operated Electric Vehicle Charging Station Map
inventory.join_role: 82 city EV charging locations; segment rows count them within 250 m
inventory.notes: Most locations are in Green P facilities (off-street). The by-law schedules add 59 current EV-charging parking rules by street name.

inventory.title: Residential Front Yard Parking
inventory.join_role: licensed front-yard and boulevard parking pads are tabulated by address (about 0.8 MB CSV) with licensed space counts; no geometry is published, and pads sit off the roadway
inventory.notes: Included because it is a parking permission the city sells; it describes the boulevard, not the parking lane.

inventory.title: Free Floating Carshare Program
inventory.join_role: the dataset has a single WEB resource and no downloadable file, so there is nothing to join; designated car-share parking areas exist as 48 current by-law rules (Schedule 43) and were joined through the rules layer
inventory.notes: A programme description page standing in for a dataset.

inventory.title: Sidewalk Inventory
inventory.join_role: shapefile-only resource (9.7 MB), inventoried for completeness; sidewalk presence borders the street parking but does not allocate it
inventory.notes: Says sidewalks are keyed to the city centreline, so a join is possible in future work.

inventory.title: Topographic Mapping – Edge of Road
inventory.join_role: the physical roadway extent as polygons (244 MB GeoJSON); inventoried, not downloaded, because it adds pavement extent only, no street parking allocation
inventory.notes: Collected from aerial photography. This is the closest public layer to the edge of the street, and it still contains no parking information.

inventory.title: Topographic Mapping – Physical area of parking lots
inventory.join_role: polygons of parking lot areas (155 MB GeoJSON); lot outlines without stall lines, prices or operators
inventory.notes: Shows that lot areas are mapped from the air while the stalls inside them are not published.

inventory.title: Topographic Mapping – Physical area of sidewalks
inventory.join_role: sidewalk area polygons; same reasoning as edge-of-road

inventory.title: One Way Streets
inventory.join_role: duplicates the one-way flag already on every centreline segment (ONEWAY_DIR_CODE_DESC), so it adds nothing to the join

inventory.title: Intersection File - City of Toronto
inventory.join_role: centreline intersection nodes; the by-law rules anchor to these IDs in 52.9% of kept rules, but the anchor is a point, not the rule's extent

inventory.title: Road Restrictions
inventory.join_role: a live feed of current closures; it says what blocks a street today, but records are point-in-time and the feed is not archived as a dataset file
inventory.notes: Useful for operations; not a stable join source.

inventory.title: Street Furniture - Transit Shelter
inventory.join_role: transit shelters stand on the sidewalk or boulevard beside the parking lane; inventoried as street furniture, not joined because shelters do not allocate the parking lane
inventory.notes: Part of a street furniture family (benches, litter bins, poster structures) published as separate datasets.

inventory.title: Street Furniture - Bicycle Parking - Bicycle Locking Ring
inventory.join_role: bicycle locking rings in the right-of-way; same reasoning as transit shelters
inventory.notes: Replaced the retired bicycle post and ring dataset.

inventory.title: Bicycle Parking Racks
inventory.join_role: multi-bike racks; same reasoning as transit shelters

inventory.title: Bicycle Post and Ring Locations
inventory.join_role: retired dataset (notes say so); replaced by street furniture bicycle parking
inventory.notes: Kept in the inventory because a search for bicycle parking still returns it.

inventory.title: Parking Lot Facilities
inventory.join_role: Parks, Forestry and Recreation parking lots; the resource is a Q3 2016 spreadsheet, nine-plus years stale

inventory.title: Private Transportation Companies - Summary and Trip Data
inventory.join_role: ride-hail trip aggregates show street parking demand (pickups and drop-offs), but trips are aggregated and the full files are yearly zips of 28-55 MB; inventoried as demand evidence
inventory.notes: Trip-level pickup points would describe street parking demand directly; the published sample is 1.3 MB.

inventory.title: Traffic Control Devices
inventory.join_role: devices are signals and related equipment, upcoming or recently activated only; it contains no parking signs
inventory.notes: Read carefully: this is the dataset a searcher expects to hold the sign inventory. It does not.

inventory.title: Traffic Signals Tabular
inventory.join_role: traffic signal, beacon and crossover locations; no parking signs

inventory.title: Turn Restrictions
inventory.join_role: retired in 2018 (notes say so); current turn rules live in the by-law schedules (Schedules 23 and 24)

inventory.title: 10 Year Cycling Network Plan – On-Street (2016)
inventory.join_role: the 2016 plan for on-street cycling routes; a plan, not the built network (bikeways carries the built network)

inventory.title: Solid Waste Daytime Curbside Collection Areas
inventory.join_role: daytime curbside collection areas; collection trucks occupy the parking lane on collection days, but the file gives areas, not days per street

inventory.title: Merged GTFS - TTC Routes and Schedules
inventory.join_role: TTC stops are street space allocations for transit; the GTFS zip carries stop points and schedules. Inventoried; a stop-level join is future work
inventory.notes: Bus loading zones also appear as 20 current by-law rules (Schedule 10) and 551 school bus loading rules (Schedule 37).

joins.method: spatial (line within 25 m) AND normalized street-name equality
joins.notes: Off-road cycling features (Multi-Use Trail*, Park Road) excluded before the join: they do not occupy a parking lane. A cycling line can match several segments. Source is the Cycling Network record (semi-annual refresh); the frozen Bikeways record carries an older, different feature set and was not used.

joins.method: spatial: segment representative point within permit-area polygon
joins.notes: 97 permit-area polygons; a segment is in an area when its midpoint falls inside.

joins.method: normalized street-name equality (rules carry no segment geometry; 30.5k of 77,940 by-law records anchor to an intersection point at best)
joins.notes: Counts attach at street level: every segment of a street carries the street's rule counts. Rule extents (side, between) stay in bylaw_rules.csv.

joins.method: street name from ticket location2 (house number stripped, first street of intersections), normalized, equality with centreline street name
joins.notes: Ticket counts attach at street level. Source files are the reference project's raw slice (6,454,695 rows of which 6,454,694 carry a valid date), not re-downloaded.

joins.join: parking occupancy -> Green P car parks
joins.method: car park number equality: Green P id '52' <-> occupancy 'CP52'; latest year/quarter kept
joins.notes: Green P snapshot is from 2019; occupancy runs to the latest published quarter. Capacity in the two files can differ; both are kept.

gaps.title: Individual paid parking stalls have no public coordinates
gaps.claim: The Toronto Parking Authority manages about 21,000 paid on-street spaces worth $67.7 million a year (TPA 2026 Operating Budget). No public dataset lists those spaces one by one: no stall coordinates, no stall boundaries, no locations for meters or pay-and-display machines. Parking policy operates at stall level (the same budget math values one lost metered spot at about $3,200 a year), and stall level is the level that is missing.
gaps.evidence: Catalogue searches on 2026-10-20 for 'stall', 'parking space', 'meter', 'pay and display', and 'curb' returned no stall inventory. The only stall-level coordinates in the catalogue are 669 accessible stalls in off-street surface lots. SenSen's published case study, 'Digitising the Streets of Toronto: AI-powered Curb Mapping' (sensen.ai), says its drive-by cameras document 'the location and state of parking signs' and identify 'physical curb assets such as meters and stalls', feeding the city's digital curb inventory for the Parking Authority. That inventory is not on open.toronto.ca.

gaps.title: Parking rules are published as legal text, not as locations
gaps.claim: Toronto publishes its street parking rules in full: 77,940 records across the schedules of Municipal Code Chapter 950. A rule names the street, the side of the street, and an extent in words ('Between a point 53 metres east of York Street and a point 36 metres east'). It does not give coordinates for where the rule starts and ends. Times and days are text strings ('Anytime', '7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., Mon. to Fri.'), so no machine can answer 'can I park on this block at 8 a.m. on Tuesday' from the published file alone.
gaps.evidence: This project streamed the dataset's single 806.5 MB JSON resource and extracted 27,768 current rules in 18 street parking categories (13,914 records are marked repealed and were dropped). 52.9% of the kept rules carry one intersection anchor point, a single lat/lon at a cross street. The other 47.1% carry no coordinates at all, and no record carries the geometry of the rule's extent. The rules therefore joined to streets by name, not to segments.

gaps.title: Snow routes are not published
gaps.claim: In the February 2025 storm, the Parking Authority closed 47% of its on-street inventory for snow removal and recorded 371,000 fewer transactions. Which streets are plowed in which order, and which parking lanes are treated as closed in a storm, is not published as data a resident or a developer can use before or during a storm.
gaps.evidence: Catalogue searches for 'snow route', 'winter maintenance', 'snow clearing', and 'plow' returned zero datasets on 2026-10-20. What exists instead is by-law text: Schedule 04 carries 2,632 winter-maintenance parking prohibitions for the former City of North York, and Schedules 17A and 17B add 176 snow-storm rules. Plow positions appear on the City's PlowTO web map during storms; the route data behind it is not in the catalogue. Storm figures: TPA 2026 Operating Budget report.

gaps.title: Occupancy is published for parking lots, not for street parking
gaps.claim: The Parking Authority publishes average daily peak occupancy for its off-street facilities, by quarter: 780 facility-quarter rows that this project joined to Green P car parks. For on-street spaces, no occupancy series exists at any level: not by stall, not by street, not by zone. Debates about whether street parking prices are too high or too low run without a published measure of how full street parking is.
gaps.evidence: The Parking Occupancy dataset's own notes limit it to off-street facilities operated by the TPA. A catalogue search for 'occupancy' returns that file and unrelated housing datasets. The joined dataset in this project can attach lot occupancy to 252 car parks; it can attach no occupancy at all to 50,027 street segments.

gaps.title: Prices are published per parking lot, as text. On-street prices are not data.
gaps.claim: Green P publishes a price for each of its 252 off-street car parks as a text string (for example '$2.50 / Half Hour'), with a numeric half-hour rate beside it. On-street paid parking, the $67.7 million a year side of the system, has no published rate table by street or zone in the catalogue. Current on-street prices live on signs, on the Green P website, and in the Green P app.
gaps.evidence: A catalogue search for 'pay and display' returned 24 keyword hits and no rate dataset. The Green P resource used here is a 2019 snapshot whose catalogue record says refresh rate 'Will not be Refreshed', so even the off-street prices in open data can be years old. Rates in the joined Green P facility file are reproduced as published, text included.

gaps.title: The parking sign inventory is not published
gaps.claim: Every street parking rule reaches a driver through a sign. The City holds a sign-level record of its streets: SenSen's system documents the location and state of parking signs for the Parking Authority, with repeat drive-bys tracking changes and obstructions. No dataset publishes parking sign locations, so a missing, faded, or contradicted sign cannot be checked against a public record.
gaps.evidence: The catalogue's Traffic Control Devices dataset covers signals and related devices, upcoming or recently activated only, and contains no parking signs. Searches for 'sign' return sign by-law districts, a third-party (billboard) sign inventory, and building-permit signs. The only public statement of the sign inventory's existence is the SenSen case study, which describes it as an operational asset of the Parking Authority.

gaps.title: Taxicab stands are published as a February 2014 spreadsheet
gaps.claim: The catalogue's taxicab stand dataset is a spreadsheet dated February 2014: 112 stands, each with a street, a side, a text location, and a stand capacity. It has no coordinates. The stands in force today exist as by-law text in Schedule 05 of Chapter 950 (159 current rules).
gaps.evidence: The file's first row states 'Toronto taxicab stand locations as of February 2014' and cites Chapter 950, Schedule 5 as its source. This project joined the current by-law rules by street name instead, and records the spreadsheet in the inventory as not joined: stale and coordinate-free.

gaps.title: Accessible parking is located for lots, not for streets
gaps.claim: Toronto publishes the coordinates of 669 accessible stalls, all of them in off-street surface lots run by the Parking Authority. No dataset locates accessible parking on the street itself, and the published by-law schedules contain no accessible-parking schedule at all.
gaps.evidence: The Off-Street Parking, Surface Lots, Accessible Stalls dataset is scoped to TPA lots in its title and notes. A search of all 190 rows of the Chapter 950 schedule tally built for this project finds no schedule for accessible or disabled parking. Accessible-permit holders park under the general permit rules; where a signed accessible space exists on a street, it is not in any public file this search found.
